title: Flourless Fudgy Brownies
summary: Deeply chocolatey brownies made without flour, held together by whipped eggs for a fudgy centre and a glossy, crackled top.
equipment: 20 cm square metal baking tin (not glass), lined with a baking-paper sling
heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat oven, line tin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan), allowing at least 20 minutes for it to come fully up to heat before baking. Line the 20cm metal tin with a baking-paper sling; a metal tin bakes more evenly than glass, which tends to leave these delicate brownies drier at the edges.

steps.title: Melt chocolate and butter
steps.text: Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring now and then until smooth. Take it off the heat and leave to cool for about 5 minutes so it won't cook the eggs later.

steps.title: Whip eggs and sugar
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar, salt and vanilla on medium-high speed for 5-6 minutes, until pale, thick and roughly doubled in volume, leaving a ribbon trail when you lift the whisk. This whipped foam does the job flour would normally do, trapping air that sets into structure and giving the shiny, crackly top.

steps.title: Combine and fold
steps.text: With the mixer on low, pour in the warm chocolate mixture in a slow stream, then fold in the sifted cocoa powder until no streaks remain. Folding gently keeps as much of that whipped air in the batter as possible.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scrape the batter into the tin, level it, and bake for 25-30 minutes. The top should look set and crackly with a centre that barely wobbles; a skewer should come out with moist crumbs rather than wet batter, and a probe reads around 90-96°C in the middle.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Cool completely in the tin, then chill for 1 hour before cutting. Flourless brownies have very little structure to hold them together while warm, so chilling firms them up enough to slice cleanly.

steps.title: Cut into squares
steps.text: Cut into 16 pieces using a hot knife, wiping the blade between cuts for neat edges.

tips: Don't skip the full 5-6 minutes of whipping the eggs and sugar — without flour to fall back on, that whipped volume gives the brownies their structure and crackly top.
Let the chocolate mixture cool before folding it in; pouring it in too hot can deflate the whipped eggs and flatten the finished brownies.
Chill before cutting rather than slicing while warm — flourless brownies are fragile until the centre firms up in the fridge.
Use a metal tin, not glass, for a more even bake; glass retains heat and can dry out the edges before the centre is set.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze the cut squares for up to 3 months. Bring back to room temperature, or warm briefly, before serving.
